newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 96/97 tapioca output seen rising 7.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai 96/97 tapioca output seen rising 7.8 pct.

text.p: Thai tapioca root production is projected to rise to 17.30 million tonnes in the 1996/97 (October/September) season from 16.06 million a year ago, the Commerce Ministry said on Monday.

Pracha Charutrakulchai, head of the ministry's foreign trade department, told reporters a field survey of 37 tapioca growing provinces this month showed that areas being planted with the crop would rise to about 1.09 million hectares during the 1996/97 year from 1.04 million a year ago.
Pracha attributed this expected 1996/97 higher output to higher tapioca prices this year.

He said of the projected 17.3 million tonnes of tapioca root, 10 million tonnes would be turned into 4.3-4.4 million tonnes of pellets and the remaining 7.3 million tonnes would be converted into 1.5 million tonnes of flour.
He said Thailand would consume 300,000-400,000 tonnes of next year's pellets, leaving an exportable surplus of four million tonnes.
Of the expected flour output, domestic demand would amount to about 750,000 tonnes with about 800,000 tonnes available for export.

Seree Denvoralak, president of the Thai Tapioca Trade Association, said the projected four million tonne pellet exportable surplus would not be sufficient to fill the 5.25 million tonne annual export quota that Thailand gets from the European Union.
He called on the commerce ministry to relax rules on allocating next year's EU quota so that private exporters could compete freely in buying tapioca from farmers.
